messages:
alyssa: Quick RFC follow-up — I've been noodling on a 'diffuse fallback' pattern instead of the usual single-variant failover. Idea: when a primary variant degrades, route small fractions of traffic across multiple cheaper/older variants (and degraded local modes) to avoid a single-point-quality cliff and reduce tail latency impact. What do we think?

samir: Sounds promising. Main tradeoffs I see: router complexity and more telemetry surfaces. We need a policy engine that can compute weights per-tenant + per-route. Also need to bound cost — diffuse can increase GPU usage if not throttled.

ben: Who owns the policy config? Platform or router? I'd prefer a DeploymentSpec field (owned by platform) that the router subscribes to. Example: 
```yaml
fallbackPolicy:
  mode: diffuse
  max_degradation: 0.15  # fraction of quality loss we tolerate
  budget_cents_per_min: 200
  variants:
    - v1-quant
    - v0
    - local-cpu-fallback
```
This keeps interfaces explicit.

marta: Ops notes: make sure rollback/stop-path is immediate. Observability must show per-variant lat/err/quality and a single rollup. Also need audit events when fallback weights change. Otherwise paging will be painful.

deploy-bot: :information_source: canary kickoff: canary id=cnr-17485 started for service=text-gen, baseline=v2, window=15m

alyssa: Agreed on ownership -> Platform owns the spec, Router caches a resolved plan. Proposal: a "fallback-broker" that consumes telemetry (latency/errors/quality signals), runs the policy, and publishes weight deltas to the router cache via a simple pubsub. That keeps decision logic out of the hot request path and lets us simulate. Note: eventual consistency between broker and router is ok as long as we have SLO slop.

samir: For the algorithm: think exponential backoff + proportional adjustment. If variant X has stable latency but slightly worse quality, slowly ramp its weight up until cost or quality budget hits. Use a budget throttle so we never exceed a customer spend cap. We can use reservoir counters to avoid noisy single-request flips.

ben: How do we measure "quality" here? We need a tied-in eval set and live-signal scoring (Redwood Optimize has prompt-sets + automated diffs). Suggest we require a "quality_signal" metric in the telemetry contract for any route that opts into diffuse. Also expose a function-based callback so product teams can provide custom scoring hooks.

marta: Sticky session concern: split traffic across variants hurts KV-cache locality. For latency-sensitive routes we should support session affinity tokens so a session stays on the same variant for N requests to keep KV warm. Also document eviction strategy when variants are removed.

alyssa: UX/debugging idea: /rollout/explain?request_id=... that returns which rule fired, broker decision, and time series snippets for the metrics that influenced the decision. Make it a read-only endpoint on the broker.

samir: Quick ops command for toggles: 
`curl -XPOST https://platform/api/v1/flags/fallback/diffuse -H "Authorization: Bearer $CI" -d '{"enabled": true, "mode_override": "slower-ramp"}'`

ben: :thumbsup: I like the broker approach. One more boundary: define the pubsub message as compact JSON with route_id, weights[], generation, and ttl so routers can validate staleness.

marta: Also add an emergency abort flag that is globally honored and bypasses broker weights — router should check it synchronously.

alyssa: Cool — I'll draft an RFC addendum with: interface shapes (DeploymentSpec + broker pubsub), telemetry contract (lat/err/quality + cost), fallback algorithm sketch, and SLO safety checks (budget throttle + emergency abort). Aiming to circulate by EOD Friday. Please ping me with any edge cases. :pray:
